text:
Maria: FYI — last night around 02:12 UTC eu-west GPUs experienced sustained queue backpressure. Tail latencies spiked and two worker pods OOM-killed and restarted.

Sam: I saw pagers. GPU util in metrics hit 97-99% and queue length climbed fast. Was there any immediate mitigation?

Devon: We throttled large-batch routes, disabled dynamic batching for rerank endpoints and routed heavy traffic to us-west for ~20m. That brought the queue down. :white_check_mark:

Maria: Key logs I pulled:
```
2026-03-17T02:12:58Z worker-42 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (runtime) total-vm: ...
2026-03-17T02:13:03Z autoscaler: scale_up request failed: InsufficientCapacity in ASG eu-west-gpu-spot
2026-03-17T02:13:20Z scheduler: queue_size=124 backlog_ms=12000
```

Katherine: Looks like two concurrent failures: (1) spot ASG didn't provide capacity when we needed it, (2) an unannounced internal load test drove KV cache growth and memory amplification leading to near-OOM on workers.

Sam: Confirmed: dev-ex ran a bigger-than-staging internal test at ~02:10 UTC and didn't use the concurrency-limited test token. We'll enforce test tokens going forward.

Devon: Autoscaler had 300s cooldown and min_headroom=0 for spot pools. When scale_up failed, requests piled up and batching increased memory retention. Also there was a recent prefix-KV eviction regression that increased per-request RAM.

Maria: Short-term mitigations applied: (1) emergency throttle for non-prod buckets, (2) route heavy requests to us-west fallback, (3) disable dynamic batching on two endpoints, (4) spin up a small on-demand reserve in eu-west to close the hole.

Sam: I'm rolling autoscaler changes: reduce scale-up cooldown to 90s, set min_headroom=2 GPUs for spot pools, and add a retry policy that prefers on-demand after N failed spot allocations. I'll own rollout.

Devon: Infra follow-ups: revert the prefix-KV eviction regression (PR queued), add hard per-pod RSS caps to avoid host OOMs, and a health-check to mark pods unhealthy if >90% RSS for 60s so scheduler can shift load earlier.

Katherine: Cost note: the temporary on-demand reserve is ~120 GPU-hours this week (~$2.4k). This is cheaper than SLA/customer impact. I'll model 0/1/2/4 GPU headroom scenarios and cost tradeoffs.

Maria: Learnings & owners:
- Root cause: unannounced heavy internal test + spot capacity shortfall + KV eviction regression -> memory amplification and near-OOM.
- Mitigations: noted above.
- Owners: Maria (incident writeup), Sam (autoscaler headroom/cooldown), Devon (runtime caps & KV fix), Katherine (cost model), Dev-ex (test token enforcement).

Dev-ex: We'll add a concurrency-limited test token and update the playbook by EOD. Apologies for the disruption.

ops-bot: Incident ticket INF-2026-0317 created and linked. :notebook_with_decorative_cover:

Maria: Scheduling a 1hr retro tomorrow 10:00 UTC to finalize timelines. I'll attach logs/graphs to the postmortem. Closing interim notes.
